record.paper_title: Semigroups of rational functions: some problems and conjectures
record.original_question: Let A and B be rational functions of degree at least two such that for every n ≥ 1 the field C(A^{∘n}) ∩ C(B) contains a non-constant rational function. Must it follow that either both A and B are special, or else there exist k, l ≥ 1 such that A^{∘2k} = A^{∘k}∘B^{∘l} and B^{∘2l} = B^{∘l}∘A^{∘k}?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.7. Let A and B be rational functions of degree at least two such that all fields (13) contain a non-constant rational function. Then either both A and B are special or there exist k, l ≥ 1 such that the equalities A^{∘2k} = A^{∘k} ∘ B^{∘l}, B^{∘2l} = B^{∘l} ∘ A^{∘k} hold.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A rational function f ∈ ℂ(z) of degree at least two is called special if it is either a Lattès map (i.e., induced by a self-map of an elliptic curve) or, up to conjugation by a Möbius transformation, equal to z^{±n} or to a Chebyshev polynomial ±T_n. For rational functions f, g ∈ ℂ(z), write f^{∘n} for the n-fold compositional iterate, and let ℂ(f) ⊆ ℂ(z) denote the subfield generated by f over ℂ.

Question: Suppose A, B ∈ ℂ(z) are rational functions, each of degree at least two, with the property that for every integer n ≥ 1 the intersection ℂ(A^{∘n}) ∩ ℂ(B) ⊆ ℂ(z) contains a non-constant rational function. Must it then be the case that either (i) both A and B are special, or (ii) there exist positive integers k, l ≥ 1 such that
   A^{∘2k} = A^{∘k} ∘ B^{∘l}   and   B^{∘2l} = B^{∘l} ∘ A^{∘k} ?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as a conjecture by Pakovich in his program on semigroups of rational functions. A web search surfaces related works of Pakovich (on amenable semigroups, generalized Lattès maps, and semiconjugate rational functions) but no source establishing the conjecture in full generality; it appears to remain open as of the available literature.

status_evidence.title: On amenable semigroups of rational functions
status_evidence.snippet: Power-twisted semigroups; relations of the form A^{∘2k} = A^{∘k} ◦ P^{∘l} studied for elements of certain semigroups.
status_evidence.claim: Related results frame the conjecture but do not resolve the general statement.

status_evidence.snippet: Listing of papers on semigroups of rational functions, Lattès maps, and field intersections.
